_comment: Curated measure→issue mappings for the Voting Record 'stance vs. record' verdict. Applied by applyCuratedIssueSeed() in netlify/lib/vr-ingest.ts. Each entry attaches to EVERY real measure with the same (congress, chamber, canonical number) that already exists — created by the seed migration or by a live Congress.gov ingest. measureType is recorded for provenance but is deliberately NOT part of the match: a live ingest that files H.Res. 1399 as a 'bill' must still receive the curated mapping, and a number that exists twice must have both rows mapped rather than one silently missed. Entries that don't match anything yet are harmless no-ops until that roll call is ingested, so nothing here can invent a measure. supportMeaning is binary: 'yea_supports' (a yea advances the issue) or 'yea_opposes' (a yea cuts against it) — see _voteEffectiveSupport in stance-helpers.js.

issues.rationale: Extends and expands the 2017 individual and business tax cuts.
Enacts net spending reductions through budget reconciliation.
Reduces federal Medicaid spending and tightens eligibility; a yea vote cuts against expanding healthcare access.
Provides new funding for border enforcement and immigration operations.
Expands onshore and offshore oil, gas, and coal leasing on federal land.
Mandates detention and removal proceedings for covered unauthorized immigrants.
Tightens immigration enforcement.

measures._comment: The bill that actually became Public Law 119-1. H.R. 29 above is the House's own Laken Riley bill, which passed the House on 2025-01-07 and went no further; the Senate took up its own S. 5, amended it, and both chambers passed that. Senate roll 119/1/7 and House roll 119/1/23 are votes on S. 5, not on H.R. 29 — see migration 20260804000000_vr_repair_laken_riley_measure_identity.sql. These four mappings are carried from H.R. 29 because the curated rationale still describes S. 5's text; the values below are byte-identical to the ones that migration inserts, because applyCuratedIssueSeed() upserts with onConflictDoUpdate and would otherwise overwrite them on the next POST /seed-issues.

issues.rationale: Mandates detention and removal proceedings for covered unauthorized immigrants.
Tightens immigration enforcement.
Triggered by arrest for burglary, theft, larceny, shoplifting, assault of a law enforcement officer, or any crime resulting in death or serious bodily injury.
issues._comment: Restated from the CRS summary of Public Law 119-1 rather than copied from H.R. 29. H.R. 29's rationale enumerates the House bill's narrower trigger list; S. 5 as enacted adds larceny and the death/serious-bodily-injury clause via the Senate amendment (roll 119/1/6, Ernst, agreed 75-24). Reusing the H.R. 29 sentence here would have understated the enacted text.

issues.rationale: Gives state attorneys general standing to sue the federal government over certain immigration-detention and enforcement decisions; a yea expands state authority to contest federal enforcement choices in court.
SAVE Act — requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.
Adds a citizenship-documentation requirement to voter registration.
Critics hold the documentation requirement narrows ballot access; a yea vote cuts against expanding voting access.
Sets the fiscal blueprint and reconciliation instructions that framed the year's tax-and-spending changes.
Directs committees to find net spending reductions through reconciliation.
Reserves reconciliation room to extend and expand the 2017 tax cuts.
Congressional Review Act resolution repealing the IRS reporting rule for decentralized-finance brokers; a yea rolls back the mandate.
Supporters framed the rule as unworkable for decentralized software and a drag on U.S. crypto development.
Reasserts congressional authority over tariffs by ending the emergency used to impose them; a yea rolls back the executive tariff action.
Removes the duties on Canadian imports; a yea favors lower trade barriers with a top trading partner.
Supporters argued the tariffs raise costs for U.S. consumers and businesses; a yea removes them.
Requires congressional authorization before military action against Iran; a yea favors restraint and a congressional check on war-making.
A yea presses against open-ended involvement in a new Middle East conflict.
Opponents held that constraining the commander-in-chief would weaken deterrence; a yea cuts against that view.
Exempts qualified tip income from federal income tax for tipped workers.
Aims to raise take-home pay for service and hospitality workers.
Reduces the federal tax burden on a category of earned income.
Repeals the waiver behind California's EV sales mandate; a yea rolls back a major state climate rule.
Supporters framed it as protecting consumer choice and gasoline-vehicle access.
Uses the Congressional Review Act to strike a federal waiver/rule.
Repeals the waiver behind California's zero-emission truck mandate; a yea rolls back a major state climate rule.
Supporters framed it as easing costs on trucking and freight.
Uses the Congressional Review Act to strike a federal waiver/rule.

Authorizes FY2026 appropriations for Department of Defense military activities, military construction, and Department of Energy defense activities (the NDAA); a yea funds and authorizes the armed forces.
Amendment (to H.R. 3944) to limit disclosures regarding earmarks; a yea reduces disclosure, cutting against transparency and anti-corruption.

Homeowner Energy Freedom Act repeals the DOE high-efficiency electric home rebate program, state home-energy contractor training grants and building energy code adoption assistance (IRA/P.L. 117-169); a yea rolls back federal climate/electrification programs.
The bill also rescinds unobligated balances for the rebate and building-energy-code programs, so a yea cancels appropriated federal spending.

Information Quality Assurance Act requires agencies to publish the critical factual material relied on in rulemaking and guidance, and to use the best reasonably available evidence; a yea expands disclosure of the government's factual basis.

Norman amendment to H.R. 3838 (FY2026 NDAA) prohibits providing gender transition procedures, including surgery or medication, through the Exceptional Family Member Program; a yea bars transgender care for military dependents.

Biggs amendment to H.R. 3838 (FY2026 NDAA) would bar designating military and certain National Guard lands as Endangered Species Act critical habitat and exempt military operations from ESA prohibitions; a yea reduces habitat protection on federal land.

Stop Insider Trading Act amends chapter 131 of title 5 to bar Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependents from holding or trading covered individual stocks; a yea is a direct vote for the congressional stock-trading ban.

Secondary: the bill's enforcement machinery is disclosure-based — advance public notice of covered transactions and published divestiture certifications — so a yea also expands financial-disclosure transparency. Weighted below the primary because the bill is not a general transparency measure.

FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act — authorizes DoD military activities, military construction, DOE defense activities, and personnel strengths; a yea funds and authorizes the armed forces. Weighted 80 rather than 100 because this NDAA also carries unrelated social-policy riders (see H.Amdt. 254-256), so passage is not a pure defense-posture signal.

Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act bars payment-card networks from requiring or assigning a merchant category code that singles out firearms retailers; a yea blocks a gun-purchase tracking mechanism that gun-rights groups oppose.
Take Care of America's Veterans Act amends titles 10 and 38 to improve veterans' benefits and VA administration; a yea expands veterans' benefits.
21st Century ROAD to Housing Act is a housing-supply package — it targets the regulatory and financing barriers to new residential construction; a yea is a vote to build more housing.
Secondary: the same package also carries affordability and federal housing-assistance provisions, so a yea advances housing affordability generally, not only new supply.

Jayapal War Powers concurrent resolution directing the President under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran; a yea ends US participation in an undeclared conflict.

Tlaib War Powers concurrent resolution directing the President under section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon; a yea ends US participation in an undeclared conflict.

Boebert amendment to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA) would codify Executive Order 14183, requiring all personnel to serve in accordance with their biological sex and thereby banning transgender service members; a yea removes an existing protection for transgender people.

Mace amendment to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA) prohibits gender-related medical care under TRICARE and bars TRICARE from covering gender-related procedures and treatments; a yea withdraws transgender health coverage.

Mace amendment to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA) prohibits male participation in female sports at Department of Defense Education Activity schools — a transgender sports-participation ban for military-dependent students; a yea restricts transgender participation.

McDowell amendment to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA) would authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish a school choice pilot program for members of the Armed Forces; a yea creates a publicly funded school-choice program.

Crank amendment to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA) establishes a presumption of approval for DoD servicemembers and civilian employees seeking their commander's authorization to carry personal firearms on military installations; a yea expands lawful carry.

Fine amendment to H.R. 8595 (FY2027 national security and State appropriations) would strike the $139,575,000 appropriation for the Global Environment Facility, the main US multilateral climate- and environment-finance channel; a yea defunds international climate finance. Weighted 75 because it is a single line item rather than a change in domestic climate policy.

Self amendment to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA) codifies protections and responsibilities for military chaplains and makes violations of those protections punishable under the Uniform Code of Military Justice; a yea strengthens statutory religious-exercise protection in the services.
Amends the Federal banking laws to widen small-business and Main Street access to capital; a yea backs that expansion of access.
Directs the Committee on Ethics to preserve and publicly release records of monetary settlements involving sexual harassment; a yea forces disclosure of settlements that are otherwise sealed.

Amends title II of the Social Security Act to reauthorize demonstration authority for the disability insurance program; a yea keeps that Social Security program authority in place. Weighted below a full-strength mapping on purpose: this is program administration, not a vote on benefit levels.
Prohibits funds appropriated by the Act from being used for Israel — a direct floor test of whether to continue a standing foreign-aid commitment.
The amendment reduces the Foreign Military Financing Program account by the corresponding amount; a yea cuts that spending.
Prohibits funds appropriated by the Act from being used for Jordan — a direct floor test of whether to continue a standing foreign-aid commitment.
The amendment reduces the National Security Investment Programs and Foreign Military Financing accounts by the corresponding amounts; a yea cuts that spending.
Ensures the continued operation of the Santa Ynez production unit; a yea keeps a domestic oil production asset online rather than letting it shut down.
The amendment's stated purpose is protecting a critical component of the military's fuel supply chain; a yea backs that supply-chain security.

Establishes a small business regulatory budget, capping the regulatory cost federal agencies may impose; a yea constrains new regulation. Identified from the H.Res. 916 rule already in this record, which describes H.R. 2965 as the small business regulatory budget bill.
The regulatory budget is scoped to the compliance burden borne by small businesses; a yea reduces that burden.

Creates an SBA hotline for small businesses to report federal rules they find burdensome; a yea backs that channel. Identified from the H.Res. 916 rule already in this record, which describes H.R. 4305 as the SBA Red Tape Hotline bill.
The hotline exists to surface federal red tape for repeal or revision; a yea advances that deregulatory review.
A Congressional Review Act resolution whose entire operative effect is to nullify a federal rule; a yea strikes the CFPB overdraft regulation off the books.

The nullified rule required very large financial institutions to cap overdraft charges at $5, justify a higher cap, or treat overdrafts as credit subject to Truth in Lending Act disclosure; a yea removes that constraint on what the largest banks may charge.

Removes Endangered Species Act protection from the San Francisco Bay-Delta longfin smelt by nullifying its listing; a yea strips a federal conservation protection. Mapped to the conservation key because the vocabulary has no dedicated wildlife or endangered-species key.
A Congressional Review Act resolution striking a federal agency rule; a yea removes the Fish and Wildlife Service regulation.
Requires public elementary and secondary schools to disclose funds received from, or contracts with, a foreign source; a yea compels disclosure that is currently not required.

Requires schools to notify parents of their right to request and receive information about foreign influence in their child's school; a yea creates a parental notification right that does not exist today.
Establishes a disclosure-on-request regime for foreign influence in schools as a condition of federal education funding; a yea widens what schools must reveal.

The FY2027 congressional budget resolution. Its published CRS summary states that it 'provides reconciliation instructions for legislation that increases the deficit', directing four House committees to report legislation increasing the deficit over FY2027-FY2036 by not more than specified amounts; a yea adopts a fiscal blueprint whose reconciliation instructions authorise deficit increases. Direction read off the summary, the mirror of the deficit-reducing instructions that set the direction on H.Con.Res. 14.

The KIDS Act requires online platforms to adopt age-identification technology on sites where a third of the content is sexual material harmful to minors, to default minors' social-media accounts to settings that limit compulsive-usage features and adult contact, to give parents account and privacy controls, and to make AI chatbots disclose their nature to minors; a yea imposes those guardrails. Mapped to the key whose own vocabulary is age verification, social media, AI and guardrails.

Part A amendment No. 1 to H.R. 8800 (FY2027 NDAA), offered by Rep. Boebert as designee for the author, Rep. Roy: 'Strike section 1213 (and redesignate accordingly).' Section 1213 amends the FY2022 NDAA to move the Afghanistan War Commission's final-report deadline from 3 years to 4, so striking it keeps the 3-year deadline and a yea insists the commission's public report arrive on the schedule Congress originally set. Weighted below a full mapping because it changes when a report is delivered, not what must be disclosed.

Part A amendment No. 44 to H.R. 8800 (Harrigan) adds 10 U.S.C. 2661(e): no federal funds may purchase, install, operate, maintain or contract for an automated speed enforcement camera system on a military installation, and any system already in operation must be decommissioned and removed within 180 days. A yea removes an automated camera-surveillance enforcement system and takes down the ones already running. Weighted low on purpose: the prohibition reaches military installations only, and the amendment expressly preserves cameras used for security, access control, force protection and criminal investigation — so it is not a vote on surveillance policy generally.

Part A amendment No. 316 to H.R. 8800 (Grothman) requires the Secretary of Defense to report within 180 days on options for reducing the number of civilians employed by the Department by 200,000, including an assessment of current non-uniformed personnel levels and recommendations for achieving the reduction while maintaining readiness. A yea asks for a plan to shrink the civilian workforce. Weighted low on purpose: the amendment commissions a report, it does not reduce anything.

The report must include 'an analysis of the anticipated cost savings associated with such reductions', so the amendment puts a 200,000-position federal payroll reduction on the table as a savings measure and a yea backs studying it. Secondary and low-weight for the same reason as the primary — this is a reporting requirement, not a cut.

Part A amendment No. 15 to H.R. 3838 (Mace, Tenney) inserts a new section barring the Superintendent of a Service Academy from allowing a cadet or midshipman who is male to participate in any athletic program or activity designated exclusively for females, with 'male' and 'female' defined by reproductive biology; a yea restricts transgender participation. Same instrument and same direction as H.Amdt. 255 (Mace, DoDEA schools) and H.Amdt. 85 (Norman, EFMP care), both already mapped at full weight. Purpose text taken from the Rules Committee report accompanying H.Res. 682, because no source we previously held carried it — see migration 20260727000000, which created this measure row deliberately without a mapping.

_phase12_overlap_priority._note: Phase 12 overlap-first ingest priorities. Point a keyed Congress.gov ingest at these issues first; each newly pulled measure should be issue-seeded to the overlap issue ONLY on a clear nexus, left unmapped otherwise. Existing seeds already cover election_integrity (H.R. 22 SAVE Act).
